a5065.speech: Said that no matter how late the technology is, it reduces labour and pollution from unwanted crops, and it increases the quality of agricultural products and the economy ; "It saves energy that is wasted during post-harvest. So far, the existing technology has been slow to save the harvested agricultural product." ; opines that farmers might take time to get used to such a new product: "Thus, the government and agricultural associations should aggressively promote it."

a5180.speaker: Finance and health experts (at the National Health Financing Policy Dialogue, Abuja)
a5180.name: Finance and health experts (at the National Health Financing Policy Dialogue
a5180.title: Abuja)
a5180.speech: Urged government at all levels to ensure that Nigeria's growing fiscal revenues are matched with accountable health spending that delivers tangible outcomes. They warned that while recent reforms have boosted public revenues, weak planning and poor execution continue to hinder health programmes, leaving citizens without real improvements in access or quality of care.

a5180.speaker: Akin Oyebode, Commissioner for Finance, Ekiti State Government and Chairman of the Forum of Finance Commissioners of Nigeria
a5180.name: Akin Oyebode
a5180.title: Commissioner for Finance, Ekiti State Government and Chairman of the Forum of Finance Commissioners of Nigeria
a5180.speech: Said Nigeria's reform agenda has boosted fiscal revenues, but warned that higher inflows must be matched with prudent spending and real outcomes. He noted that the fiscal compact between federal, state and local governments is an important milestone, but warned that sudden increases in inflows could trigger inflationary pressures if not carefully managed. “Higher inflows are welcome, but if they are not translated into executed expenditure, they are just numbers on paper.”

a5180.speaker: Akin Oyebode, Commissioner for Finance, Ekiti State Government
a5180.name: Akin Oyebode
a5180.title: Commissioner for Finance, Ekiti State Government
a5180.speech: Highlighted weaknesses in existing health programmes, particularly nutrition initiatives, which he described as fragmented and poorly coordinated; added that while social programmes such as school feeding were important, they must be scaled nationally to deliver impact. He also flagged the growing challenge of health-workers migration, driven by widening pay disparities across states, saying in some places up to 20 per cent of staff are leaving because of uneven pay. “Without a stable workforce, primary health care will remain weak, no matter how much money is put in.”

a5180.speaker: Muyi Aina, Executive Director of the National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA)
a5180.name: Muyi Aina
a5180.title: Executive Director of the National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA)
a5180.speech: Warned that Nigeria's health costs are rising faster than available budget revisions, citing vaccines as an example and noting that even with the most rigorous forecasts, year-on-year costs for essential commodities such as childhood immunisation, TB medicines and programme operations continue to escalate. He stressed that while the federal, state and local governments are constitutionally required to co-finance primary health care, actual contributions remain inconsistent, creating gaps in service delivery. “With resources tied, and costs rising, we must maximise the value of every naira spent. That means efficiency, transparency and accountability must go hand in hand with new money.” ; He proposed several options to expand fiscal space, including the full implementation of at least one per cent of the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF), targeted domestic levies, and efficiency reforms: “Donors and partners can support, but Nigeria must first demonstrate its own commitment.”

a5180.speaker: Iziaq Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a5180.name: Iziaq Salako
a5180.title: Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a5180.speech: Had on Monday said that the ministry is considering legislation to double BHCPF funding from one to two per cent of consolidated revenue. Mr Salako said the federal government has consistently funded the BHCPF and introduced emergency allocations to cushion the suspension of foreign aid.

a5481.speaker: Kamina Johnson Smith, Jamaica's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade
a5481.name: Kamina Johnson Smith
a5481.title: Jamaica's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade
a5481.speech: Has publicly expressed profound gratitude to the Government of Eswatini for its cooperation and the duty of care exercised in facilitating the safe and voluntary repatriation of deportee Orville Isaac Etoria to Jamaica: "We are pleased to welcome home Mr Etoria and we trust the Jamaican public understands and joins the government in respecting his desire for a quiet return."

a5481.speaker: Kamina Johnson Smith, Jamaica's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade
a5481.name: Kamina Johnson Smith
a5481.title: Jamaica's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade
a5481.speech: Emphasised that the well-being of Jamaicans overseas remains a constant priority for the Government of Jamaica and noted that this case serves as another clear example of the importance of international cooperation and the critical role played by Jamaica's diplomatic network in protecting the rights of its citizens abroad ; extended thanks not only to Eswatini but also to the International Organisation for Migration (IOM) for its direct support, as well as to Jamaica's High Commission in Pretoria for their hands-on engagement: "Together, our combined efforts ensured Mr Etoria's safe return."

a5505.speaker: Mahamoud Omar Guelleh, Director(-General) of ANEFIP
a5505.name: Mahamoud Omar Guelleh
a5505.title: Director(-General) of ANEFIP
a5505.speech: Thanked the representatives of the major local hotels for their constant support for the training of young jobseekers ; reiterated to the young jobseekers that they should take advantage of this training opportunity offered by the Ministry of Labour.

a5505.speaker: Christopher Snipes, Charge d'affaires of the US Embassy in Djibouti
a5505.name: Christopher Snipes
a5505.title: Charge d'affaires of the US Embassy in Djibouti
a5505.speech: Recalled that the hotel industry in Djibouti, and more generally the hospitality sector, offers growing employment prospects: “It is a sector where one learns and develops essential professional skills such as teamwork, problem-solving and decision-making. It is an ideal place to start a career.” ; stressed that “Djiboutians who take part in USAID's youth employment programme receive intensive training, practical training in the hotel sector and a practical transition in order to succeed in the labour market. These practical training opportunities are fundamental. This is not theoretical learning, but real experience. The programme is designed to ensure that future employees - I am speaking of you who are taking part in the programme, you, the future employees - adapt quickly to the world of work and meet the rigorous standards of the private sector.”

a5505.speaker: Omar Abdi Said, Minister of Labour, in charge of formalisation and social protection
a5505.name: Omar Abdi Said
a5505.title: Minister of Labour, in charge of formalisation and social protection
a5505.speech: Paid vibrant tribute to the staff of the Ministry of Labour, to USAID, to E.D.C. and to the general management of the Kempinski hotel, as well as all those who contributed to shaping the human capital consolidation programme ; congratulated the certified young beneficiaries and urged them to go on learning: “To our young graduates, my most sincere congratulations. You have acquired valuable skills, but remember that learning is a continuous journey. Keep training, innovating and reaching new heights.”

a5505.speaker: Omar Abdi Said, Minister of Labour, in charge of formalisation and social protection
a5505.name: Omar Abdi Said
a5505.title: Minister of Labour, in charge of formalisation and social protection
a5505.speech: In his address, said that over the past weeks he had met representatives of various economic sectors to understand the expectations of professionals, and that the previous consultations made it possible to establish a shared diagnosis of the skills deficit in key sectors of the economy and to identify strategic interventions to respond to unmet demands ; said that the qualification of human resources is crucial to achieving a high level of competitiveness for businesses and that it is therefore imperative to develop a public-private partnership to put in place training aligned with the labour market and the standards of the national economy, adding that this training was the fruit of the very first public-private partnership, made possible by the cooperation between ANEFIP and the general management of the Kempinski hotel, which allowed the training to be delivered on the hotel's premises by its own employees.

a5659.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Prime Minister of Somalia
a5659.name: Hamza Abdi Barre
a5659.title: Prime Minister of Somalia
a5659.speech: Last week voiced his support for Hamas, a Palestinian armed group, during a religious event at the newly renovated national theatre in Mogadishu.

a5659.speaker: African Union Transition Mission in Somalia (ATMIS) and the Frontline States Task Force
a5659.name: African Union Transition Mission in Somalia (ATMIS) and the Frontline States Task Force
a5659.speech: Have agreed to strengthen collaboration in the fight against Al-Shabaab.

a5659.speaker: Muse Bihi Abdi, President of Somaliland
a5659.name: Muse Bihi Abdi
a5659.title: President of Somaliland
a5659.speech: Reiterated his commitment to defending the borders of Somaliland, including the region of Laascaanood, while urging Dhulbahante elders to engage in negotiations.

a5659.speaker: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
a5659.name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
a5659.speech: Welcomed a €25 million contribution from the Government of Germany to provide access to food and other basic goods and services while protecting and restoring productive livelihoods in drought-affected communities in Ethiopia.

a5659.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM) and 47 other partners
a5659.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM) and 47 other partners
a5659.speech: Are appealing for USD 84 million to provide humanitarian and development assistance to over 1 million migrants and the communities hosting them, many of whom are vulnerable, and in need.

a5659.speaker: Committee of Ambassadors of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)
a5659.name: Committee of Ambassadors of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)
a5659.speech: Convened and endorsed the IGAD Budget 2023 on the budget of the regional organisation for the year 2023.

a5750.speaker: Rasheedat Ajibade, Super Falcons Captain
a5750.name: Rasheedat Ajibade
a5750.title: Super Falcons Captain
a5750.speech: Has outlined what Nigeria must do to evolve from continental champions to FIFA Women's World Cup winners; speaking to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) after the team's reception by President Bola Tinubu at the State House on Monday, said there was need for structural support for the team; said the team's recent WAFCON triumph in Morocco proved they can aim higher if given the right backing; called for urgent investment in facilities, professional conditions, and tournament preparation to elevate the team's global standing: "We want to be global contenders, not just local champions. We have dominated in Africa and it is time to take it to the world stage. So, all we need to do is just support and to keep promoting women football and set the platform for generations to come. When we talk of support, I am talking about proper preparations for tournaments and proper professional conditions for players."

a5750.speaker: Rasheedat Ajibade, Super Falcons Captain
a5750.name: Rasheedat Ajibade
a5750.title: Super Falcons Captain
a5750.speech: Said that the warm reception from President Tinubu was a major morale boost that could inspire greater achievements.

a5750.speaker: Rasheedat Ajibade, Super Falcons Captain
a5750.name: Rasheedat Ajibade
a5750.title: Super Falcons Captain
a5750.speech: On the team's vision and the support sought: "Our vision is bold. We want to become the best women's football team in the world. We dream of standing at the top of the global stage, not just as competitors, but as champions." ; "To achieve this, we only seek the continued and enhanced support of the NFF, NSC and the Federal Government. With your partnership, we can have world-class training facilities, and we will be able to prepare in the best way possible, and create a pathway for the next generation of Super Falcons to score even higher. Together, we can show the world that Nigeria is not just a participant in global football, but a leader."

a5940.speaker: Alain Godonou, Chief of Mission for Heritage and Museums to Beninese President Patrice Talon
a5940.name: Alain Godonou
a5940.title: Chief of Mission for Heritage and Museums to Beninese President Patrice Talon
a5940.speech: Explains the museum's architecture: “It evokes many things, it recalls that hint of calabashes, an important element in Vodun culture broadly speaking. We also highlight Batammariba architecture, commonly called ‘tata somba’.”

a5940.speaker: Alain Godonou, Chief of Mission for Heritage and Museums to Beninese President Patrice Talon
a5940.name: Alain Godonou
a5940.title: Chief of Mission for Heritage and Museums to Beninese President Patrice Talon
a5940.speech: Recounts that the museum will display objects from abroad: “Here and there, we are in discussions with partners. Sometimes the discussions are concluded so as to obtain objects significant to Vodun culture, notably Vodun culture coming from outside the continent.”

a5940.speaker: Alain Godonou, Chief of Mission for Heritage and Museums to Beninese President Patrice Talon
a5940.name: Alain Godonou
a5940.title: Chief of Mission for Heritage and Museums to Beninese President Patrice Talon
a5940.speech: Said the aim is to show Vodun in all its components: “the objective is to manage to strip Vodun of the negative ideas attributed to it. And for the public to discover that Vodun is entirely respectable.”

a5940.speaker: Alain Godonou, Chief of Mission for Heritage and Museums to Beninese President Patrice Talon
a5940.name: Alain Godonou
a5940.title: Chief of Mission for Heritage and Museums to Beninese President Patrice Talon
a5940.speech: Describes the works under way: “There will be a circulation route. It will be protected, we will build a canopy. There, the workers are making the foundations of the canopy elements, so that the walk inside the museum is protected.”

a5940.speaker: Alain Godonou, Chief of Mission for Heritage and Museums to Beninese President Patrice Talon
a5940.name: Alain Godonou
a5940.title: Chief of Mission for Heritage and Museums to Beninese President Patrice Talon
a5940.speech: Is confident the timetable can be met: “the major works are finished. The finishing works have begun. The museology and museography are progressing very well. You are never safe from a surprise, but I firmly believe that by the end of 2025, it will be able to open.”

a5987.speaker: Lebohang Makhoali, Petroleum Fund Head of Operations
a5987.name: Lebohang Makhoali
a5987.title: Petroleum Fund Head of Operations
a5987.speech: Said the Fund faces significant challenges, including the illegal importation of fuel from neighbouring countries; complained about companies involved in the ongoing Lesotho Highlands Water Project (LHWP) Phase II in Mokhotlong which he said had found ways to bring fuel into the country illegally for their operations, bypassing the required revenue payments, though he was unable to provide an estimate of losses; said the workshop was designed to give the officers a foundational understanding of the petroleum industry and related laws ; “There is a new challenge that we are facing, particularly in the northern region, because of the ongoing LHWP II. Many companies involved in the project are using illegal methods to import fuel, resulting in significant revenue losses for the government” ; “We set new fuel prices every month, but some businesses do not comply. After we send inspectors to ensure compliance, many return to their original prices once the inspection is over, especially in the case of illuminating paraffin.”

a5987.speaker: ‘Makananelo Thato Kome, Petroleum Fund Chief Executive Officer
a5987.name: ‘Makananelo Thato Kome
a5987.title: Petroleum Fund Chief Executive Officer
a5987.speech: Said they had already partnered with district administrators as part of the effort to combat these issues, and that the collaboration is meant to ensure that fuel sellers comply with the laws that protect consumers, the environment, and the nation as a whole ; “Since our offices are in Maseru, we realised the need to collaborate with government departments in the districts. We’ve initiated relationships with district administrators, informing them about the Petroleum Fund and the challenges we face in our work, especially our responsibility to set fuel prices each month. We expect those selling fuel to comply with the prices set by the Petroleum Fund, but our offices are not located in the districts or rural areas. That’s why we’ve decided to partner with the LMPS to help enforce the rules and regulations governing the fuel industry” ; “We invite the LMPS to work closely with us to ensure that businesses adhere to the legal requirements of the fuel industry.”

a5987.speaker: Sera Makharilele, Deputy Commissioner of Police (LMPS)
a5987.name: Sera Makharilele
a5987.title: Deputy Commissioner of Police (LMPS)
a5987.speech: Stated that it was imperative for the police to be afforded such a crucial training, citing the importance of understanding industry-specific issues to identify irregularities; also mentioned the prevalence of people selling fuel from containers at unreasonable prices ; “For a police officer to be considered professional, they need to be familiar with the systems they are enforcing. When dealing with issues that affect the nation, it’s critical to have a thorough understanding of them. Issues relating to fuel impact the Basotho nation, and anything that affects Basotho also affects us as police officers. Our responsibility is to ensure that people are not cheated by criminals and can live comfortably. Our role is to enforce the law, and in order to do that, we need to be aware of key details. This partnership between the Petroleum Fund and LMPS is crucial because it helps us protect Basotho livelihoods. As the world changes, new challenges arise, which the LMPS must address. Today’s workshop is important because it equips us to recognise abnormalities in the fuel industry” ; “As the LMPS, we need to be proactive in addressing these issues and gather the necessary information from this workshop to take decisive action.”

a6170.speaker: Khadija Hassan Mohamed, Somali refugee and traditional house plasterer in Dadaab
a6170.name: Khadija Hassan Mohamed
a6170.title: Somali refugee and traditional house plasterer in Dadaab
a6170.speech: Noted that the few people building preferred to use corrugated iron sheets, and that she used to earn 10-15,000 Kenya shillings a month, which was sufficient for their basic needs; told Radio Ergo’s local reporter: “When the work stopped, the family’s situation significantly worsened. There’s no income and the situation is very complicated. I just sit at home; I can’t afford the food we used to cook, and we can’t sustain ourselves. It’s like a heavy burden has fallen on us. When I can’t afford anything and can’t provide, I just sit alone and talk to myself” ; “I just wander around the town. If I find laundry work, I do it, and in the evening that’s how I cook for them. If I don’t find any, I rely on God. That’s how we live. Sometimes, after bathing the children, I just put them to sleep. In the morning, without having cooked anything for them, I go look for work again.”

a6170.speaker: Khadija Hassan Mohamed, Somali refugee and traditional house plasterer in Dadaab
a6170.name: Khadija Hassan Mohamed
a6170.title: Somali refugee and traditional house plasterer in Dadaab
a6170.speech: On her children being expelled from school in June because they could not pay the 400 shillings per child for school supplies: “The children are without education. They’re just sitting at home. We couldn’t afford it when the children told us, Mum, I don’t have a pen, I don’t have a bag. When we had money, we used to buy those pens, books, and bags for them including uniforms, and everything they needed for their schooling.”

a6170.speaker: Faduma Abdiqadir Khamis, traditional house plasterer in Dadaab
a6170.name: Faduma Abdiqadir Khamis
a6170.title: traditional house plasterer in Dadaab
a6170.speech: Told Radio Ergo: “Since my work stopped, my life has severely declined. It was good before but now we have nothing. My children and I just look at each other! We live on cooked food that our relatives give us. Last night and the night before, I didn’t cook anything, and even now I have nothing to cook. They go to bed hungry and wake up hungry.”

a6170.speaker: Faduma Abdiqadir Khamis, traditional house plasterer in Dadaab
a6170.name: Faduma Abdiqadir Khamis
a6170.title: traditional house plasterer in Dadaab
a6170.speech: Explained that she had fallen ill due to strenuous work and anxiety, fainted in May while washing clothes and was taken to the camp hospital, where she was diagnosed with high blood pressure and diabetes: “I became sick with high blood pressure. I fell sick doing the laundry work. When my sickness worsened, I gave up have to and stay at home” ; “My blood pressure is very high. My children and I have given up hope and we have a big problem on that front – no food, no clothes, and no schooling for the children.”

a6170.speaker: Amina Abdiqadir Ali, head of women’s empowerment, Women Lead Steering Committee
a6170.name: Amina Abdiqadir Ali
a6170.title: head of women’s empowerment, Women Lead Steering Committee
a6170.speech: Said 200 women house plasterers had been out of work since the beginning of the year, and that refugee women and youth were currently facing the worst level of unemployment ever in Dadaab, as contracts with aid organisations had ended and casual labour jobs had shrunk: “Women who used to go out at dawn and do manual labour, washing laundry, plastering houses, sweeping yards, or running restaurants, have all stopped. The women who used to plaster houses and wash clothes, their work has stopped as such jobs are no longer found in the camps” ; added that the youth finishing school were jobless, and the cuts in humanitarian aid meant that many families were going without cooking meals.

a6204.speaker: Mohammed Manga, Director of Information and Public Relations (signed statement)
a6204.name: Mohammed Manga
a6204.title: Director of Information and Public Relations (signed statement)
a6204.speech: According to the statement signed by Manga, the $747 million syndicated loan to fund Phase 1, Section 1 of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway was arranged by Deutsche Bank, which served as the Global Coordinator, Initial Mandated Lead Arranger, and Bookrunner, and which also participated in the lending syndicate alongside other regional and international financiers; Manga noted that Phase 1, Section 1 of the project covers the stretch from Victoria Island to Eleko Village in Lagos.

a6204.speaker: Federal Ministry of Finance (statement)
a6204.name: Federal Ministry of Finance (statement)
a6204.speech: Described the financing as Nigeria’s first syndicated loan of such magnitude for road infrastructure, highlighting it as a sign of strong global investor confidence in the country’s reform agenda and infrastructure pipeline. The statement read, “The Islamic Corporation for the Insurance of Investment and Export Credit (‘ICIEC’) provided partial political and commercial risk insurance. The syndicate includes support from development finance institutions, export credit agencies and international commercial banks—notably First Abu Dhabi Bank, also acting as Agent across all facilities and Intercreditor Agent, whose involvement underscores its strong and growing support for Nigeria. Other lenders involved are the African Export-Import Bank (‘Afrexim’), the Abu Dhabi Exports Office (‘ADEX’), the ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (‘EBID’), Nexent Bank N.V. (formerly known as Credit Europe Bank N.V.) and Zenith Bank (through its UK, Paris and Nigeria offices). The project is structured as an EPC+F (Engineering, Procurement, Construction + Financing) contract awarded to Hitech Construction Company, one of Nigeria’s leading infrastructure firms.”

a6204.speaker: Mohammed Manga, Director of Information and Public Relations
a6204.name: Mohammed Manga
a6204.title: Director of Information and Public Relations
a6204.speech: “This structure aims at a strategic partnership between the Government and the private sector, seamlessly aligning technical execution with financing solutions,” he said; according to Manga, it will enable fast-track project delivery while unlocking and maximising private sector appetite for investment in the country’s priority infrastructure. He stated that the construction of Phase 1, Section 1, is already over 70% complete, and explained that the highway, constructed using Continuously Reinforced Concrete Pavement (CRCP), was a reflection of a commitment to long-term resilience and efficiency. “Engineered for a minimum lifespan of 50 years with minimal maintenance, it offers outstanding durability and cost-effectiveness,” he said. “The project’s design and implementation have been shaped by comprehensive technical, legal, and environmental and social assessments, ensuring alignment with the highest international standards.”

a6204.speaker: Wale Edun, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a6204.name: Wale Edun
a6204.title: Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a6204.speech: “This deal reflects the success of our macroeconomic reforms and the return of international capital to support Nigeria’s development. We are focused on financing infrastructure in ways that are sustainable, transparent, and catalytic—and this transaction is a model of that vision in action. The closing of this market defining financing is yet another testament to Mr President’s commitment to accelerate the participation of the private sector in infrastructure financing and development. It positions the country as being ready for a full transition to the design, development, financing as well as operations and management of critical public infrastructure through Public Private Partnerships, PPPs.” ; “It signals to investors and private sector participants, the sophistication and maturity of the Nigerian market and commitment of the government to sanctity of contracts and innovative structures to fund critical national infrastructure that will deliver sustained and inclusive growth,” he added.

a6353.speaker: Nigerian Senate
a6353.name: Nigerian Senate
a6353.speech: Has allocated additional N300 billion to the health sector in the 2025 approved budget to bridge the gap created by the United States government's freeze on foreign aid; the Senate said the funds would support health interventions and address challenges previously financed by US government foreign aid before its suspension.

a6353.speaker: Health experts
a6353.name: Health experts
a6353.speech: Worry that Nigeria's health sector could face significant challenges without US foreign aid.

a6353.speaker: Nigerian government
a6353.name: Nigerian government
a6353.speech: Had pledged to strengthen the health sector and intensify domestic funding to ensure ownership and sustainability of the country's HIV/AIDS response; announced it would begin producing tools such as test kits and antiretroviral drugs locally.

a6353.speaker: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a6353.name: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a6353.speech: Said the US executive orders had made the re-evaluation of the country's dependence on foreign aid a necessary move.

a6353.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES (earlier reporting)
a6353.name: PREMIUM TIMES (earlier reporting)
a6353.speech: PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the government had pledged to strengthen the health sector and intensify domestic funding to ensure ownership and sustainability of the country's HIV/AIDS response; this paper also reported that the government had announced it would begin producing tools such as test kits and antiretroviral drugs locally.

a6475.speaker: Reverend Billy Gamah, chairperson of the Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a6475.name: Reverend Billy Gamah
a6475.title: chairperson of the Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a6475.speech: Declared that, based on the partial presidential results announced by the Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC), “the table cannot change to deliver victory” for Chakwera ; “A public statement by the President acknowledging defeat would not only be an act of statesmanship but also a powerful gesture to encourage his supporters to accept the outcome peacefully.” ; “We believe that conceding early, even before the official announcement, will show maturity, promote peace, and help the nation move forward without violence or unnecessary tension.”

a6475.speaker: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a6475.name: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a6475.speech: Says the responsible path for Chakwera is to publicly concede and call for calm among his supporters.

a6475.speaker: Bakili Muluzi, former president of Malawi
a6475.name: Bakili Muluzi
a6475.title: former president of Malawi
a6475.speech: Confirmed that he had personally urged Chakwera to concede and call Mutharika to congratulate him; argued that doing so would defuse political tensions and safeguard Malawi’s democratic stability, reminding Chakwera that “there is life after State House.”

a6475.speaker: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC)
a6475.name: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC)
a6475.speech: Announced the partial presidential results last night, showing former president Peter Mutharika commanding an unassailable lead in 21 out of the 24 councils tallied.

a6526.speaker: Malawi's officials, including the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Treasury
a6526.name: Malawi's officials
a6526.title: including the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Treasury
a6526.speech: Remain in the dark about the implications of the suspension of U.S. foreign aid.

a6526.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Lilongwe
a6526.name: U.S. Embassy in Lilongwe
a6526.speech: Has indicated it needs more time to assess the orders' potential impact.

a6526.speaker: Milward Tobias, Economist
a6526.name: Milward Tobias
a6526.title: Economist
a6526.speech: Points out that Malawi's position in U.S. priorities post-review remains unclear, leaving the nation vulnerable to funding cuts.

a6539.speaker: Adam Kuhlmann, Mariental mayor
a6539.name: Adam Kuhlmann
a6539.title: Mariental mayor
a6539.speech: Said council will strive to provide quality and affordable services for its residents with the current financial year’s budget; said the budget made provision for overall expenditure of over N$127 million against a total estimated operating income of N$127.7 million; “Allow me to make a specific remark regarding council finances. It must be noted that the 2021/2022 budget of council is 95% self-funded”; said the town council is mostly relying on electricity and water sales and assessment rates, with these accounting for the biggest portion of its revenue; expressed concern over the fact that general and staff expenses are taking up 85% of the budget, which might in the end put pressure on revenue collection.

a6539.speaker: Adam Kuhlmann, Mariental mayor
a6539.name: Adam Kuhlmann
a6539.title: Mariental mayor
a6539.speech: “Council was forced to minimally increase sanitation and sewerage tariffs between seven and eight percent to cushion the rising cost of repairs and maintenance to the ageing network assets.”

a6539.speaker: Adam Kuhlmann, Mariental mayor
a6539.name: Adam Kuhlmann
a6539.title: Mariental mayor
a6539.speech: “Council also awarded an inflationary salary increase of 3% for staff, as the last salary increase was in 2019”; expressed his appreciation to staff for their patience and goodwill shown in this regard; “It is the considered view of the town council that the staff members’ wellbeing and satisfaction is paramount in the delivery of services and eventual customer satisfaction.”

a6539.speaker: Adam Kuhlmann, Mariental mayor
a6539.name: Adam Kuhlmann
a6539.title: Mariental mayor
a6539.speech: Said as a means to further enhance service delivery, the municipality has devised an appropriate Covid-19 response to install pre-paid water meters, and further resolved to implement zero rate basic water charges for senior citizens: “Council will also implement a special rate on electricity for senior citizens that will save them 32 cents per electricity unit cost”; reported that for this year, council envisages to install 1 000 pre-paid water meters and build 200 toilets in the Takarania, Donkerhoek and Ombili informal settlements in town.

a6539.speaker: Adam Kuhlmann, Mariental mayor
a6539.name: Adam Kuhlmann
a6539.title: Mariental mayor
a6539.speech: On the issue of housing, said it was council’s aim to work with strategic partners in order to build houses for qualifying ultra-low-income earners: “We intend to redirect a portion of funds earmarked for debt servicing towards the construction of low-cost housing units.”

a6610.speaker: Amnesty International (report, "ETHIOPIA: THE NEED FOR AN INDEPENDENT INTERNATIONAL INVESTIGATION OF THE AXUM MASSACRE")
a6610.name: Amnesty International (report
a6610.title: "ETHIOPIA: THE NEED FOR AN INDEPENDENT INTERNATIONAL INVESTIGATION OF THE AXUM MASSACRE")
a6610.speech: Their evidence indicated that most of the victims of the massacre were unarmed civilian residents of Axum, many of whom were attempting to flee the violence. ; The report findings continued that it is clear from witness statements that Eritrean soldiers killed civilians in front of their family members, including children, during their house-to-house raids, and that the soldiers are reportedly guilty of attacking friends and relatives of the victims who tried to collect the bodies of those killed.

a6610.speaker: Witnesses interviewed by Amnesty International
a6610.name: Witnesses interviewed by Amnesty International
a6610.speech: Confessed that it is Eritrean soldiers who went on a rampage, shooting at civilian men and youths who were out on the streets attempting to flee. ; Confirmed that rather than shooting fighters, Eritrean soldiers shot at men who posed no threat to them, and that some of the Axum massacre victims carried no weapons and in many cases were running away from the soldiers when they were shot.

a6610.speaker: Ethiopian Attorney General's Office (report)
a6610.name: Ethiopian Attorney General's Office (report)
a6610.speech: Minimized the role of the Eritrean forces in the massacre, claiming that the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) fighters had distributed Ethiopian and Eritrean military uniforms to criminals released from prison.

a6610.speaker: Mark Lowcock, UN humanitarian chief
a6610.name: Mark Lowcock
a6610.title: UN humanitarian chief
a6610.speech: In a statement to the media, said that Ethiopian lives and livelihoods were being destroyed by drought, and children were suffering from malnutrition. Noting that six months into the conflict in Tigray, civilians continued to bear the brunt. Women and girls were being targeted with horrific sexual violence, and millions were struggling to access essential services and food, especially in some rural areas that were completely cut off. That is why there was the need to scale up the humanitarian response immediately.

a6610.speaker: United Nations
a6610.name: United Nations
a6610.speech: Observed that the ongoing humanitarian response throughout Ethiopia, especially in Tigray, remains insufficient to meet the needs of most of the affected people, and that more funding is needed, alongside safe and unfettered humanitarian access, to ensure aid organizations and the Ethiopian Government can scale up to the level needed.

a6610.speaker: Addis Ababa Standard (report)
a6610.name: Addis Ababa Standard (report)
a6610.speech: Published a report that was a stark contrast to what Amnesty International alongside other international human rights organizations had reported, especially on the identity of the victims and the role of Eritrean troops in the killing of civilians.

a6619.speaker: Investigators
a6619.name: Investigators
a6619.speech: Say that the attacker who opened fire on pupils as they were praying at a church in Minneapolis was "obsessed with the idea of killing children".

a6619.speaker: Brian O'Hara, Minneapolis Police Chief
a6619.name: Brian O'Hara
a6619.title: Minneapolis Police Chief
a6619.speech: Said Robin Westman, who killed two children and injured 18 others, did not seem to have any specific motive. The attacker "appeared to hate all of us", the chief said on Thursday, adding: "More than anything, the shooter wanted to kill children". ; He added that she, "like so many other mass shooters that we have seen in this country too often and around the world, had some deranged fascination with previous mass shootings".

a6619.speaker: Brian O'Hara, Minneapolis Police Chief
a6619.name: Brian O'Hara
a6619.title: Minneapolis Police Chief
a6619.speech: Told reporters that news outlets should stop using the killer's name, because "the purpose of the shooter's actions was to obtain notoriety".

a6619.speaker: Relative of Fletcher Merkel (unnamed)
a6619.name: Relative of Fletcher Merkel (unnamed)
a6619.speech: "Fletcher loved his family, friends, fishing, cooking and any sport that he was allowed to play," he said. "Give your kids an extra hug and kiss today. We love you, Fletcher. You'll always be with us," he continued, choking back tears.

a6619.speaker: Michael Moyski and Jackie Flavin, parents of Harper Moyski (statement)
a6619.name: Michael Moyski and Jackie Flavin
a6619.title: parents of Harper Moyski (statement)
a6619.speech: Said in a statement that their daughter "was a bright, joyful, and deeply loved 10-year-old whose laughter, kindness, and spirit touched everyone who knew her". "As a family, we are shattered, and words cannot capture the depth of our pain," they said, adding that they hope "her memory fuels action" to stop gun violence. "No family should ever have to endure this kind of pain.... Change is possible, and it is necessary - so that Harper's story does not become yet another in a long line of tragedies."

a6619.speaker: Joseph Thompson, acting US Attorney General for Minnesota
a6619.name: Joseph Thompson
a6619.title: acting US Attorney General for Minnesota
a6619.speech: In a news conference on Thursday said "the shooter expressed hate towards many groups, including the Jewish community and towards President Trump". ; "I won't dignify the attacker's words by repeating them, they are horrific and vile," said Mr Thompson.

a6619.speaker: Officials
a6619.name: Officials
a6619.speech: Said the attacker, who died at the scene of a self-inflicted gunshot wound, left a note, but added that a definitive motive may never be known. ; In their news conference, officials confirmed that the attacker had previously attended the school, and that three residences associated with the attacker have been searched by police. They said that the church locked its doors before beginning its Mass service, likely saving many lives. Officials added that the guns used in the attack were all legally purchased, that the killer did not appear on any government watchlist, and that police are not aware of any mental health diagnoses or treatments that she was receiving.

a6619.speaker: Judge in Westman's 2020 name-change case (court record)
a6619.name: Judge in Westman's 2020 name-change case (court record)
a6619.speech: Westman's name was legally changed from Robert to Robin in 2020, with the judge writing: "Minor child identifies as a female".

a6619.speaker: US officials
a6619.name: US officials
a6619.speech: Have warned for years that mass shooting can lead to copycat killings, as killers seek to become famous through their heinous crimes.

a6619.speaker: Kash Patel, FBI Director
a6619.name: Kash Patel
a6619.title: FBI Director
a6619.speech: Has described the attack as "an act of domestic terrorism motivated by a hate-filled ideology". In a post on X, Patel said that the attacker "left multiple anti-Catholic, anti-religious references" written on guns and in notes uncovered by investigators. "Subject expressed hatred and violence toward Jewish people, writing Israel must fall,' 'Free Palestine,' and using explicit language related to the Holocaust," he wrote. The killer also "wrote an explicit call for violence against President Trump on a firearm magazine".

a6619.speaker: Mary Grace Westman, the attacker's mother (non-response)
a6619.name: Mary Grace Westman
a6619.title: the attacker's mother (non-response)
a6619.speech: Her mother, Mary Grace Westman, previously worked at the school, and has so far not responded to law enforcement's attempts to contact her.

a6619.speaker: Patrick Scallen, resident living near the church
a6619.name: Patrick Scallen
a6619.title: resident living near the church
a6619.speech: Said that he saw three children fleeing the building - one of them a girl with a head wound. "She kept saying, 'please hold my hand, don't leave me', and I said I wasn't going anywhere."

a6619.speaker: Vincent Francoual, father of an 11-year-old who was in the church
a6619.name: Vincent Francoual
a6619.title: father of an 11-year-old who was in the church
a6619.speech: Said he tried not to panic after he heard the news. He called it "sick" that children in the US are trained to prepare for mass shootings. "We live in a country where we train kids what to do. And she did what she had to do," he said. "Here it's a pattern. It's no longer a freak accident," he said of school shootings in the US. "I told my wife that every morning, when we drop our kids, we don't know if she'd be back safe." ; Said that Chloe is afraid to return to school or church.

a6619.speaker: Jacob Frey, Minneapolis Mayor
a6619.name: Jacob Frey
a6619.title: Minneapolis Mayor
a6619.speech: "There is no reason that someone should be able to reel off 30 shots before they even have to reload," said Mayor Jacob Frey, also calling for a ban on high-capacity ammo magazines. "We're not talking about your father's hunting rifle here. We're talking about guns that are built to pierce armour and kill people."

a6728.speaker: Vivian van de Perre, deputy head of MONUSCO
a6728.name: Vivian van de Perre
a6728.title: deputy head of MONUSCO
a6728.speech: Briefed journalists from Goma on the ongoing crisis, emphasising that the situation remains volatile, with the risk of further escalation, and warned: “Military action alone will not resolve this conflict.”

a6728.speaker: Vivian van de Perre, deputy head of MONUSCO
a6728.name: Vivian van de Perre
a6728.title: deputy head of MONUSCO
a6728.speech: “Some 2,000 people—both UN personnel and Congolese civilians—are sheltering within our premises”, with pressure growing on essential resources including water, food and sanitation.

a6728.speaker: MONUSCO (UN peacekeeping mission in the DRC)
a6728.name: MONUSCO (UN peacekeeping mission in the DRC)
a6728.speech: Has expressed grave concern over the potential takeover of Kavumu airport, warning that losing both airports amid the ongoing humanitarian crisis would be disastrous for the region.

a6728.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6728.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6728.speech: Has raised alarms about potential disease outbreaks, as the bodies of over 2,000 people have already been buried, with 900 still in morgues, raising fears of an epidemic.

a6728.speaker: Vivian van de Perre, deputy head of MONUSCO
a6728.name: Vivian van de Perre
a6728.title: deputy head of MONUSCO
a6728.speech: Confirmed the presence of Rwandan forces in eastern DR Congo, despite denials from the Rwandan government.

a6728.speaker: Rwandan government
a6728.name: Rwandan government
a6728.speech: Has denied the presence of Rwandan forces in eastern DR Congo.

a6728.speaker: Unnamed reports cited by the article
a6728.name: Unnamed reports cited by the article
a6728.speech: Reports have pointed to Rwandan military involvement alongside M23 fighters; reports also indicate that M23 has ordered NGOs to halt operations in areas under their control, further limiting humanitarian access.

a6728.speaker: Vivian van de Perre, deputy head of MONUSCO
a6728.name: Vivian van de Perre
a6728.title: deputy head of MONUSCO
a6728.speech: Stressed the need for “clear guidance” from the UN Security Council, as the situation continues to evolve rapidly.

a6728.speaker: Stéphane Dujarric, UN spokesperson
a6728.name: Stéphane Dujarric
a6728.title: UN spokesperson
a6728.speech: “We urgently call for the reopening of Goma airport. We need to evacuate the wounded and bring in critical humanitarian supplies and staff.”

a6728.speaker: Vivian van de Perre, deputy head of MONUSCO
a6728.name: Vivian van de Perre
a6728.title: deputy head of MONUSCO
a6728.speech: Emphasised the need for a political solution: “The people of the DRC deserve peace, security, and stability”, urging all parties to end the fighting, prioritize dialogue, and work toward a peaceful resolution.

a6818.speaker: Ghana School Feeding Programme (GSFP) Secretariat (press statement)
a6818.name: Ghana School Feeding Programme (GSFP) Secretariat (press statement)
a6818.speech: “The GSFP Secretariat, under the supervision of the MoGCSP, has commenced a restructuring of the programme to fulfil the government’s commitment to decentralise its operations, improve the quality of food served and ensure consistency in the payment of caterers,” the secretariat said in a statement. The statement further announced that the government, through the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP), had paid the 31 days’ arrears owed to caterers under the GSFP for the first term of the 2024/2025 academic year.

a6818.speaker: Hajia Fati Forgor, National Coordinator of the GSFP Secretariat (press statement)
a6818.name: Hajia Fati Forgor
a6818.title: National Coordinator of the GSFP Secretariat (press statement)
a6818.speech: thanked the government for the release of funds for the payment of the outstanding arrears. “The GSFP Secretariat extends its appreciation to the government for the timely release of funds for the payment of outstanding arrears owed to the caterers,” the statement read.

a6818.speaker: Ghana School Feeding Programme (GSFP) Secretariat
a6818.name: Ghana School Feeding Programme (GSFP) Secretariat
a6818.speech: expressed gratitude to the programme’s donor partners for their support, indicating that such collaborations remained vital to the sustainability of the initiative. “We thank our donor partners for their continuous support and collaboration with the Government of Ghana to sustain the programme,” it said.

a6818.speaker: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Finance Minister (Ghana)
a6818.name: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson
a6818.title: Finance Minister (Ghana)
a6818.speech: Presenting the Budget Statement to Parliament on March 11, 2025, announced an increase in the feeding grant per child from GH¢1.20 to GH¢1.60. He explained that the increment was necessitated by rising food prices and the need to sustain the programme to ensure that pupils in public basic schools continued to receive nutritious meals.

a6829.speaker: Jonathan Said, AGRA’s Vice President and Head of its Centre of Technical Expertise
a6829.name: Jonathan Said
a6829.title: AGRA’s Vice President and Head of its Centre of Technical Expertise
a6829.speech: Told Nyasa Times after a recent visit that Malawi has “a once-in-a-generation opportunity” to restructure its agriculture sector and reduce its heavy reliance on tobacco and tea for foreign exchange: “Soybeans and groundnuts have the potential to be larger than tobacco in terms of forex earnings and to create youth work opportunities on a large scale.” ; “If Malawi can coordinate across government, private sector and farmer groups, export revenue could double in the next 5–10 years.”

a6829.speaker: Jonathan Said, AGRA’s Vice President and Head of its Centre of Technical Expertise
a6829.name: Jonathan Said
a6829.title: AGRA’s Vice President and Head of its Centre of Technical Expertise
a6829.speech: Noted: “These value chains are critical not just for export earnings, but also for nutrition, soil health, women’s empowerment and climate adaptation.”

a6829.speaker: Jonathan Said, AGRA’s Vice President and Head of its Centre of Technical Expertise
a6829.name: Jonathan Said
a6829.title: AGRA’s Vice President and Head of its Centre of Technical Expertise
a6829.speech: Stressed: “You cannot have commercialization and agro-industrialisation without anchor firms.” ; “And you cannot build competitive value chains without fixing seed supply.”

a6829.speaker: Jonathan Said, AGRA’s Vice President and Head of its Centre of Technical Expertise
a6829.name: Jonathan Said
a6829.title: AGRA’s Vice President and Head of its Centre of Technical Expertise
a6829.speech: Believes the presidency must play a central convening role in driving this transformation: “The presidency has the power to align actors and keep focus on solving bottlenecks in extension, seeds, digitalisation, mechanisation and finance.” ; “We’ve seen glimpses of this through the President’s Delivery Unit and the National Planning Commission, but it needs to be accelerated.”

a6829.speaker: Jonathan Said, AGRA’s Vice President and Head of its Centre of Technical Expertise
a6829.name: Jonathan Said
a6829.title: AGRA’s Vice President and Head of its Centre of Technical Expertise
a6829.speech: Despite challenges such as climate change and volatile global markets, is upbeat: “Malawi has all the ingredients. With leadership, focus and coordination, agriculture can finally become the engine of inclusive growth that Malawians have long been waiting for.”

a6920.speaker: Public Health Institute of Malawi
a6920.name: Public Health Institute of Malawi
a6920.speech: Said the newly identified patients range in age from 17 to 41, and that health officials are investigating how the infections were transmitted and are currently tracing contacts.

a6920.speaker: Spokesperson from the Public Health Institute of Malawi (anonymous)
a6920.name: Spokesperson from the Public Health Institute of Malawi (anonymous)
a6920.speech: "We are working to understand the source and halt further spread."

a6920.speaker: Experts
a6920.name: Experts
a6920.speech: Have warned that the Mpox surge could be worsened by weakened immune systems among people living with HIV, particularly following recent cuts in foreign aid.

a6920.speaker: Richard Mvula, spokesperson for the Lilongwe District Health Office
a6920.name: Richard Mvula
a6920.title: spokesperson for the Lilongwe District Health Office
a6920.speech: "Some of those affected by Mpox were immunocompromised."

a6920.speaker: UNAIDS
a6920.name: UNAIDS
a6920.speech: Earlier cautioned that the aid cuts would have immediate repercussions for HIV programmes in Malawi, including increased vulnerability to other infectious diseases like Mpox.

a6920.speaker: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a6920.name: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a6920.speech: Reports over 52,000 cases and at least 1,770 deaths continent-wide since January.

a6920.speaker: Officials
a6920.name: Officials
a6920.speech: Say more than six million vaccine doses are needed urgently, but less than a quarter of that number is currently available.

a6920.speaker: Steven Banda, taxi driver in Lilongwe
a6920.name: Steven Banda
a6920.title: taxi driver in Lilongwe
a6920.speech: "I only found out from a Ministry of Health official. She explained the symptoms and warned us to be cautious. But I haven't seen anyone sick in my area."

a6920.speaker: Health officials
a6920.name: Health officials
a6920.speech: Warn that a lack of public knowledge mirrors the early days of Covid-19 in the country, when misinformation led many to turn to unproven herbal remedies.

a6920.speaker: Dr. Victor Mithi, President of the Society of Medical Doctors
a6920.name: Dr. Victor Mithi
a6920.title: President of the Society of Medical Doctors
a6920.speech: Called for heightened alertness among healthcare professionals: "We need to integrate Mpox screening into routine procedures. This virus can spread rapidly in our communities, especially where people live in close quarters and practice physical greetings like handshakes and hugs."

a6920.speaker: Dr. Victor Mithi, President of the Society of Medical Doctors
a6920.name: Dr. Victor Mithi
a6920.title: President of the Society of Medical Doctors
a6920.speech: Added that although the country gained valuable public health experience during Covid-19, the healthcare system's current state, strained by resource cuts, is a major concern: "Without sustained support, especially following the pullout of U.S. aid, we're operating in survival mode. More than half of our healthcare funding comes from donors, and the bulk of that was from the United States. Our system is vulnerable."

a6997.speaker: Dr. Jarso Jallah, Liberian Education Minister
a6997.name: Dr. Jarso Jallah
a6997.title: Liberian Education Minister
a6997.speech: Has emphasized that the construction of dormitories and a resource center at the Technical Center for Professional Training, Research, and Innovation (TCPTRI) at BWI in Kakata is more than just an infrastructure, but a strategic investment in Liberia's youth and future ; extended heartfelt thanks to the European Union and the Government of Sweden for their co-funding support, calling the partnership a shared commitment to education, skills training, and empowering our youth for job creation and sustainable development.

a6997.speaker: Dr. Jarso Jallah, Liberian Education Minister
a6997.name: Dr. Jarso Jallah
a6997.title: Liberian Education Minister
a6997.speech: Reaffirmed the government's commitment to fast-tracking the Litcom Bill, which aims to strengthen the legal and institutional framework for TVET in Liberia.

a6997.speaker: Nathaniel McGill, Margibi County Senator and Chair of the Senate Committee on Education
a6997.name: Nathaniel McGill
a6997.title: Margibi County Senator and Chair of the Senate Committee on Education
a6997.speech: Expressed deep excitement and national pride at the groundbreaking ceremony ; praised the resilience of the campus leadership and the dedication of Education Minister Jarso Jallah, acknowledging the challenges of leading the Education Sector in a politically dynamic environment ; emphasized that education must transcend political divisions and be embraced as a national priority ; addressed skepticism from some quarters about his presence at the event, given his position in the opposition, clarifying that his support for the initiative is rooted in a shared national vision, not partisanship.

a6997.speaker: Nathaniel McGill, Margibi County Senator
a6997.name: Nathaniel McGill
a6997.title: Margibi County Senator
a6997.speech: Linked the importance of the new facilities to broader social challenges, including youth vulnerability and drug abuse, stressing that without institutions like TCPTRI, many young Liberians lack alternatives and opportunities for a better life.

a6997.speaker: Dr. Anna Brososowska, EU Team Leader
a6997.name: Dr. Anna Brososowska
a6997.title: EU Team Leader
a6997.speech: Reaffirmed the European Union's unwavering commitment to investing in Liberia's human capital, describing it as the most valuable and sustainable path to national development ; emphasized that the EU's support is rooted in a long-term vision for empowering Liberia's youth ; highlighted the importance of retaining trained educators within Liberia, ensuring that the benefits of education are reinvested into local communities ; stressed the EU's commitment to gender equality, noting that the initiative aims to open doors for girls and women in fields traditionally dominated by men ; expressed optimism about the pending legislation, citing successful models in Kenya and Zambia where similar commissions have transformed national education systems into regional training hubs.

a7090.speaker: Elie Kalkoumdo, new Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a7090.name: Elie Kalkoumdo
a7090.title: new Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a7090.speech: "We are taking on the post of Director General of Customs at a pivotal moment, when there are great challenges linked to the issue of optimal revenue mobilisation and trade facilitation, in a context in which the Head of State and the government are engaged in the fight against terrorism. I do not doubt for a single moment the support of my hierarchical superiors and the backing of all my fellow customs officers in meeting the challenges assigned to us. My wish is that within the customs house there be solidarity, commitment and harmony." ; He also saluted all of customs' collaborators and partners.

a7090.speaker: Adama Sawadogo, outgoing Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a7090.name: Adama Sawadogo
a7090.title: outgoing Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a7090.speech: Urged customs agents to close ranks around their new boss: "Keep in mind that the starting point of any undertaking is desire, and that few things remain impossible for those who are always at work." ; Expressed all his joy at having worked with each of his collaborators and paid tribute to the customs agents who, despite prejudices and other stereotypes, work hard for revenue mobilisation.

a7090.speaker: Adama Sawadogo, outgoing Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a7090.name: Adama Sawadogo
a7090.title: outgoing Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a7090.speech: Confided that customs revenues had almost doubled during his five-year term: "This was possible thanks to the reforms we undertook, notably with the Virtual Link System for Import and Export Operations (SYLVIE), the satellite monitoring of all of Burkina Faso's corridors and the scanner system project." ; Added that revenues went from single to double also because the administration worked to standardise the behaviour of economic operators through IT tools.

a7224.speaker: Ministers of Djibouti (Moustapha Mohamed Mohamoud, Radwan Abdillahi Bahdon and Dr Nabil Mohamed Ahmed, at a press briefing)
a7224.name: Ministers of Djibouti (Moustapha Mohamed Mohamoud
a7224.title: Radwan Abdillahi Bahdon and Dr Nabil Mohamed Ahmed, at a press briefing)
a7224.speech: Finally, a press briefing hosted by high-school students allowed the ministers to share their impressions of these memorable events, underlining the importance of education and culture in building a bright future for the Djiboutian nation.
